verses.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!

xrefs.text: from Edom and Moab, from the Ammonites and Philistines and Amalekites, and from the spoil of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, who had marched out to restore his dominion along the Euphrates River.
But You have rejected and humbled us; You no longer go forth with our armies.
As far as Hamath, David also defeated King Hadadezer of Zobah, who had marched out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River.
So David went to Baal-perazim, where he defeated the Philistines and said, “Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me.” So he called that place Baal-perazim.

verses.text: You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.

xrefs.text: and if My people who are called by My name humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
Come, let us return to the LORD. For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.

The light of the moon will be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter— like the light of seven days— on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King. The earth quakes at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His indignation.
I will seek the lost, bring back the strays, bind up the broken, and strengthen the weak; but the sleek and strong I will destroy. I will shepherd them with justice.’

verses.text: You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.

xrefs.text: Though You have shown me many troubles and misfortunes, You will revive me once again. Even from the depths of the earth You will bring me back up.
Awake, awake! Rise up, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His fury; you who have drained the goblet to the dregs— the cup that makes men stagger.
Thus says your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people: “See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering. From that goblet, the cup of My fury, you will never drink again.
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: “Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink from it.
Because you have followed the path of your sister, I will put her cup into your hand.’

verses.text: You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah

xrefs.text: May we shout for joy at your victory and raise a banner in the name of our God. May the LORD grant all your petitions.
He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold— how speedily and swiftly they come!
He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.

verses.text: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.

xrefs.text: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.
Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
Show the wonders of Your loving devotion, You who save by Your right hand those who seek refuge from their foes.
You have given me Your shield of salvation; Your right hand upholds me, and Your gentleness exalts me.

verses.text: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.

xrefs.text: and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon (the territory on the east side of the Jordan up to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth
Once and for all I have sworn by My holiness— I will not lie to David—
Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: “Behold, the days are coming when you will be taken away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.

verses.text: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.

xrefs.text: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.

His majesty is like a firstborn bull, and his horns are like those of a wild ox. With them he will gore the nations, even to the ends of the earth. Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh.”
half of Gilead; and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan. All this was for the clans of the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, that is, half of the descendants of Machir.

Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh as Joseph’s firstborn son, namely for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh and father of the Gileadites, who had received Gilead and Bashan because Machir was a man of war.

Some from Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. (They did not help the Philistines because the Philistine rulers consulted and sent David away, saying, “It will cost us our heads if he defects to his master Saul.”)

verses.text: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.

xrefs.text: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.
He placed garrisons throughout Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Gath and its villages from the hand of the Philistines.
Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines. But David became exhausted.

verses.text: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?

xrefs.text: Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.

In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel. They destroyed the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah, but David remained in Jerusalem.
David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
Now David had said, “Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander.” And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief.
And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”

verses.text: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?

xrefs.text: This is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They will turn their backs and run from their enemies, because they themselves have been set apart for destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove from among you whatever is devoted to destruction.
Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
But the LORD said to me, “Tell them not to go up and fight, for I am not with you to keep you from defeat by your enemies.”

For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”

verses.text: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.

xrefs.text: Put not your trust in princes, in mortal man, who cannot save.
Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
A song of ascents. Of David. If the LORD had not been on our side— let Israel now declare—
Egypt’s help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
And He will redeem Israel from all iniquity.

verses.text: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.

xrefs.text: Through You we repel our foes; through Your name we trample our enemies.
Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”

“I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with Me. I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury; their blood spattered My garments, and all My clothes were stained.
And from His mouth proceeds a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and He will rule them with an iron scepter. He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.
Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
